Implement by updating the weight decay value in the optimizer param group each step next to the existing LR/momentum schedule update.

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 so grad accumulation halves and the model gets about twice as many optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s. backlog.spec: Make Muon's cautious weight decay follow WEIGHT_DECAY * (1 - progress), where progress is the fraction of the 300 s time budget used. Compute it each step next to the LR schedule and write it into the Muon param groups. Nothing else changes. This reduces the late-training regularization drag during warmdown.

backlog.spec: For the first 30% of the time budget, train on sequences truncated to half length. Use a fixed set of shapes to avoid repeated recompiles; if the model is compiled, mark it dynamic=False and accept one recompile. Early steps get cheaper, so there are more steps in the budget.

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP with a gated SiLU unit: gate and up projections each of hidden size round(8/3*dim) rounded to a multiple of 64, and a down projection back to dim. Output is down(silu(gate(x))*up(x)). Keep the down projection zero-init like the current one. Parameter count stays about the same as the 4x ReLU^2 MLP. Muon handles all three matrices.

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN so all layers use the short window (half context) except the final layer, which stays full. For example, use a pattern string of 'SSSSSSSL' for depth 8, assuming the code forces the last layer to be long. Cheaper attention means more steps in the fixed time. Check that the window-size construction handles the string.

backlog.spec: Find the logit softcap constant applied to the final logits, as in softcap*tanh(logits/softcap). It is probably 15 or 30. Set it to 10. This tests how much the bound limits the model and how it affects the loss. Change only this constant.
backlog.title: Logit softcap lowered to 10

backlog.spec: After the Muon orthogonalization step, keep a per-row EMA (beta 0.95) of the squared update values, with one scalar per output row. Divide each row by sqrt(EMA)+eps. Then rescale the whole update so its overall Frobenius norm matches the pre-normalization norm. This equalizes neuron update sizes. Implement it inside the Muon step with one extra buffer per parameter, about ten lines.
backlog.title: NorMuon-style per-row second-moment scaling

backlog.spec: Use a smaller batch early. Set grad accumulation steps so the first 25% of the time budget uses TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE/4 tokens per optimizer step, then 2x for the next 25%, then the full 2**19. Scale the loss by the current number of micro-steps. Keep LR unchanged. This gives many more early updates when gradients are noisy-insensitive and costs no extra code complexity beyond a step-size function.
backlog.title: Batch-size ramp

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary loss that predicts the token two positions ahead from the final hidden states. Reuse the tied or untied lm_head on hidden states normed through a small learnable linear map of size dim x dim, initialized to zero plus identity residual. Compute cross entropy against targets shifted by one more position, ignoring the last position. Add it with weight 0.3 during the first 70% of the time budget, then 0 for the end. Evaluation is unchanged because only the main head is used.

memo: Incumbent is now mean_adjusted 1.0504 over 2 runs. The one clear win was slot 13: cutting TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**17 gave 1.0533/1.0475 (-0.0642). It carries a tripwire flag, so check that before building on it. More optimizer steps in a fixed 300 s is the main lever. Everything after it failed to beat the incumbent: SwiGLU (1.0529, +0.0025) and WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7 (1.0520, +0.0016). Earlier small tweaks were within noise. Failures: warmup (+0.0111), DEPTH 10 (+0.0487), and combining UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.008 with warmdown 0.3 (+0.0011). Slots 8 and 9 (EMA, attention-kernel swap) crashed. Many slots were wasted on aborted no-change ideas, so check train.py first. Next: replicate the incumbent to settle the tripwire and noise. Then try smaller batches (2**16), re-tune LR for the new batch size, and retry UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.008 on its own. Prefer throughput gains over architecture changes.
